jah.def: The Rastafari name of God, a short form of Jah/Yah drawn from YHWH (Yahweh) and the biblical 'Jah' of Psalm 68:4. In Iyaric it is the living, personal name of the Almighty, often identified by Rastafari with Haile Selassie I.

ini.def: 'I and I' (InI), the central Rastafari first-person pronoun. It replaces both 'I', 'me', 'we' and 'us' to express that the individual and JAH (and all people) are unified as one divine presence, dissolving the separation between self and others.

irated.def: Iyaric (Rastafari 'I-word') form of 'created.' Rastafari speech replaces syllables that sound negative or that hide the divine 'I' with 'I', so 'created' becomes 'Irated,' affirming JAH as the creating power.

irator.def: Iyaric coinage for 'Creator,' used as a title of JAH. The prefix 'I' asserts the divine first-person presence within the word for the maker of all things.

irie.def: Iyaric word meaning good, right, pleasing, or at peace; a state of positive well-being and harmony with JAH. One of the core 'I-words' of Rastafari speech.

iration.def: Iyaric form of 'creation,' the created world or the act of creating, reframed to carry the divine 'I' rather than the 'c' sound.

irations.def: Plural Iyaric form of 'creation(s)' — created things or created works, spoken to carry the divine 'I' of JAH.

itority.def: Iyaric form of 'authority,' the rightful power and rule, rebuilt around the divine 'I' rather than the 'au' sound.

ites.def: Iyaric form of 'heights,' meaning the high or heavenly places, exaltation, or a joyful elevated state; from replacing 'height' with the uplifting 'I' sound.

iginnin.def: Iyaric form of 'beginning,' the origin or first time, spoken to open with the divine 'I' sound.

iternity.def: Iyaric form of 'eternity,' endless time or everlasting life, reframed around the divine 'I'.

inity.def: Iyaric form of 'unity,' the oneness of InI and JAH and of all people; from replacing 'u' with the divine 'I'.

inited.def: Iyaric form of 'united,' made one; from replacing 'u' with the divine 'I'.

ipointed.def: Iyaric form of 'appointed,' meaning set in place or chosen by JAH; the 'a' is replaced by the divine 'I'.

ipoint.def: Iyaric form of 'appoint,' to set in place or ordain, reframed with the divine 'I'.

judgemant.def: Iyaric spelling of 'judgment,' the divine act of judging. Rastafari speech often reshapes word endings, and here the '-ment' becomes '-mant' while keeping the sense of JAH's judgment.

fiyah.def: Iyaric/Jamaican-patois form of 'fire,' often used for the purifying, judging fire of JAH that consumes wickedness.

hola.def: Iyaric/patois form of 'holy' (or a hailing greeting), used to mark what is set apart and sacred to JAH. Sense in this text is somewhat uncertain.

faada.def: Iyaric/Jamaican-patois pronunciation of 'Father,' used of JAH as the divine Father.

downstruction.def: Iyaric form of 'destruction.' Rastafari word-play replaces the 'de-' (which sounds like 'death/down-putting') with the more truthful 'down-,' so ruin is spoken as 'downstruction.'

mek.def: Jamaican-patois/Iyaric form of 'make' or 'let,' as in 'mek InI' (let us / make us).

unu.def: Jamaican-patois/Iyaric second-person plural pronoun, 'you' (plural, 'all of you'); of West African (Igbo) origin.

becaudis.def: Iyaric/patois rendering of 'because (of this)' — a dialect contraction. Exact form in the text is uncertain.

amen.def: Hebrew liturgical word meaning 'so be it' or 'truly,' spoken to affirm and seal a prayer, blessing, or statement of truth.

isra'iel.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Israel — both the patriarch Jacob (renamed Israel) and the covenant nation and land descended from him, the people to whom JAH gave the Law.

israel.def: The covenant people and land of the twelve tribes descended from Jacob (Israel); in scripture the nation chosen by God, and figuratively the community of the faithful.

iyerusaliem.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Jerusalem, the holy city of Israel, site of the Temple and the seat of David's kingdom.

jerusalem.def: The holy city of Israel, capital of David's kingdom and site of the Temple; center of Jewish worship and, symbolically, the city of God.

gehannem.def: Gehenna, the place of fiery punishment for the wicked (hell). The name derives from the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, once a site of idolatrous child-sacrifice, which became a symbol of divine judgment and torment.

babylon.def: The great Mesopotamian empire and city on the Euphrates that conquered Judah and destroyed the Temple (586 BC), carrying the Jews into exile. In scripture and in Rastafari usage it symbolizes worldly, oppressive, corrupt power set against JAH.

sion.def: Zion, the hill of Jerusalem and the city of God; symbolically the dwelling place of JAH and the promised home of the redeemed, a central image in Rastafari faith.

egypt.def: The ancient kingdom on the Nile where Israel was enslaved before the Exodus under Moses; in scripture a symbol of bondage and the worldly power from which JAH delivers His people.

judea.def: Judaea, the southern land of the tribe of Judah around Jerusalem, the heartland of the Jewish people after the exile.

jewry.def: An older English term for the land of Judea or the Jewish people/community collectively.

juda.def: Judah — either the patriarch, the leading tribe descended from him, or the southern kingdom/land of Judah around Jerusalem.

judah.def: The fourth son of Jacob, the tribe descended from him, and the southern kingdom of Judah with its capital at Jerusalem; the royal line of David and, by tradition, the Messiah.

yihuda.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Judah — the tribe, land, or kingdom of Judah.

mo`ab.def: Moab, the kingdom east of the Dead Sea whose people descended from Lot; a frequent rival and sometime oppressor of Israel.

moab.def: Moab, the kingdom east of the Dead Sea, descended from Lot; often at war with Israel in the scriptures.

edom.def: Edom, the mountainous land south of the Dead Sea settled by the descendants of Esau, Jacob's brother; a recurring enemy of Israel.

edomyas.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Edom, the land of Esau's descendants south of Judah, and its people the Edomites.

edomites.def: The descendants of Esau who inhabited Edom; a neighboring and often hostile people to Israel.

sedom.def: Sodom, the city near the Dead Sea destroyed by fire from heaven for its wickedness, together with Gomorrah; a byword for sin and divine judgment.

gemorra.def: Gomorrah, the city destroyed alongside Sodom by fire from heaven for its wickedness; a symbol of corruption and judgment.

sorya.def: The Ge'ez/Ethiopic form of Syria, the region to the north of Israel around Damascus.

syria.def: The region and kingdom north of Israel centered on Damascus; at times an enemy and at times an overlord of the Jews.

demasqo.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Damascus, the chief city of Syria north of Israel.

damascus.def: The ancient capital city of Syria, north of Israel.

celosyria.def: Coele-Syria ('Hollow Syria'), the region between the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon mountain ranges, named in the Greek apocrypha.

phenice.def: Phoenicia, the coastal land north of Israel (Tyre and Sidon), famed for its seafaring merchants.

libanus.def: The Latin/Greek name for Lebanon, the mountain range and cedar-forest region north of Israel.

hama.def: Hamath, an ancient city-state on the Orontes River in Syria, north of Israel.

theeros.def: Likely the Ge'ez rendering of Tyre, the great Phoenician port city on the Mediterranean coast. Identification is somewhat uncertain.

bethulia.def: The Israelite hill town, guarding the passes to Jerusalem, besieged by the Assyrian army in the Book of Judith and delivered when Judith slew the general Holofernes.

nineve.def: Nineveh, the great capital of the Assyrian Empire on the Tigris; setting of much of the Book of Tobit and the target of Jonah's preaching.

ecbatane.def: Ecbatana, the capital of Media (in modern Iran); a setting in the Book of Tobit where Raguel and Sara lived.

rages.def: An ancient Median city (near modern Tehran) mentioned in the Book of Tobit, where Gabael held Tobit's money in trust.

media.def: Media, the land and empire of the Medes in northwestern Iran, allied with Persia against Babylon.

persia.def: The Persian Empire founded by Cyrus the Great, which overthrew Babylon and permitted the Jews to return and rebuild the Temple.

fars.def: Fars (Persis), the southern Iranian homeland of the Persians; here used for Persia itself.

elam.def: Elam, the ancient kingdom east of Babylon (in southwestern Iran), with its capital at Susa; also the name of a son of Shem.

assur.def: Asshur/Assur, the ancestor and homeland of the Assyrians and their chief god; used for Assyria, the empire that destroyed the northern kingdom of Israel.

assyrians.def: The people of the empire of Assyria, centered on Nineveh, who conquered the northern kingdom of Israel and, in the Book of Judith, besieged Bethulia under Holofernes.

mesopotamia.def: The land 'between the rivers' (Tigris and Euphrates), the region of Babylon and Assyria, ancestral homeland of Abraham.

euphrates.def: One of the two great rivers of Mesopotamia, flowing past Babylon; one of the four rivers of Eden in Genesis.

tigris.def: One of the two great rivers of Mesopotamia, running past Nineveh; one of the four rivers of Eden (Hiddekel) in Genesis.

chaldeans.def: The Chaldeans, the people of southern Babylonia who ruled the Neo-Babylonian Empire under Nebuchadnezzar; also used for astrologers and the land of Abraham's birth (Ur of the Chaldees).

chaldees.def: Chaldea, the region of southern Babylonia; Abraham came from 'Ur of the Chaldees.'

sinai.def: Mount Sinai (Horeb), the mountain where JAH gave Moses the Law and the Ten Commandments.

hermon.def: Mount Hermon, the high mountain on Israel's northern border; in the Book of Enoch the peak where the two hundred Watchers descended and swore their oath to sin.

chanaan.def: Canaan, the Promised Land west of the Jordan given to Israel; the Greek/older spelling of Canaan.

kene`an.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Canaan, the Promised Land given to Israel.

kenaniewon.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of the Canaanites, the peoples inhabiting the land of Canaan before Israel.

gele`ad.def: Gilead, the fertile highland region east of the Jordan River, known for its balm; territory of the tribes of Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh.

midyam.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Midian, the desert land where Moses fled and married; home of the Midianites, later enemies of Israel.

miedon.def: Likely a Ge'ez rendering of Midian, the desert people and land east of the Gulf of Aqaba. Identification is uncertain.

ammon.def: Ammon, the kingdom east of the Jordan descended from Lot; the Ammonites were frequent enemies of Israel (Achior in Judith is their captain).

amalieq.def: Amalek, the nomadic desert people descended from Esau who attacked Israel after the Exodus and became a symbol of implacable enmity against God's people.

amalieqans.def: The Amalekites, the people of Amalek, a nomadic nation and perennial enemy of Israel.

philistines.def: The seafaring people of the coastal plain of Canaan (from Gaza, Ashkelon, etc.), Israel's great enemies in the days of Samson, Saul and David; Goliath was their champion.

gentiles.def: The nations, that is, all non-Jewish peoples; those outside the covenant of Israel.

levites.def: The members of the tribe of Levi, set apart to serve at the Temple and assist the priests (who were the Levitical house of Aaron).

levi.def: The third son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the priestly tribe of Levi (the Levites) and of the priesthood of Aaron.

jews.def: The people of Judah and, more broadly, the whole covenant people of Israel who kept the Law of Moses; named from the kingdom of Judah.

israelites.def: The people of Israel, the twelve tribes descended from Jacob (Israel).

egyptians.def: The people of Egypt, who enslaved Israel before the Exodus.

medes.def: The people of Media, allied with the Persians in overthrowing Babylon.

persians.def: The people of Persia, whose empire under Cyrus freed the Jews from Babylonian exile.

benjamin.def: The youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, and the tribe descended from him; Tobit and Mordecai are of this tribe in the apocryphal books.

ephraim.def: A son of Joseph and the leading tribe of the northern kingdom; also used for the hill country and the northern kingdom of Israel itself.

nephthali.def: Naphtali, a son of Jacob and the northern tribe descended from him; Tobit belonged to the tribe of Naphtali.

watchers.def: In the Book of Enoch, the two hundred angels ('the Watchers') who descended on Mount Hermon, took human wives, fathered the giants, and taught forbidden arts, bringing corruption to the earth and judgment upon themselves.

meqabees.def: The Meqabyan/Maccabee figures of the Ethiopic Books of Meqabyan. Note these Ethiopian 'Maccabees' (centered on the martyr-hero and his people) differ from the Greek Books of Maccabees; the name evokes the Maccabean resistance to pagan oppression.

meqabyan.def: The Books of Meqabyan (1, 2 and 3 Meqabyan), Ethiopic scriptures canonical in the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Bible. They are distinct from the Greek Books of Maccabees and recount faithful resistance to godless kings.

meqabyans.def: The people/heroes of the Books of Meqabyan, or the books themselves; the Ethiopic 'Maccabees' who resisted ungodly rule.

adam.def: The first man, formed by JAH from the earth and placed in the Garden of Eden; through his sin death entered the world. Father of the human race.

hiewan.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Eve (Hewan), the first woman, made from Adam and mother of all the living.

qayel.def: The Ge'ez form of Cain, the eldest son of Adam and Eve who murdered his brother Abel and became the first man to shed blood.

qayen.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Cain, first son of Adam and murderer of his brother Abel.

siet.def: Likely the Ge'ez form of Seth, the third son of Adam and Eve, born after Abel's death and ancestor of the righteous line. Identification is somewhat uncertain.

enoch.def: The seventh from Adam, son of Jared and father of Methuselah, who 'walked with God and was not, for God took him' (Genesis 5). Traditional author of the Book(s) of Enoch, in which he receives visions of heaven, the Watchers, and the final judgment.

jared.def: A patriarch in the line of Seth, son of Mahalalel and father of Enoch; in the Book of Enoch it was in his days that the Watchers descended.

mahalalel.def: An antediluvian patriarch in the line of Seth, son of Cainan and father of Jared.

methuselah.def: Son of Enoch and grandfather of Noah; the longest-lived man in scripture (969 years). Enoch addresses much of his book to Methuselah.

lamech.def: Son of Methuselah and father of Noah in the righteous line of Seth (distinct from the earlier Lamech of Cain's line).

noah.def: The righteous man whom JAH preserved with his family in the ark through the Flood, becoming the second father of humanity; son of Lamech and great-grandson of Enoch.

noh.def: A variant spelling of Noah, the righteous man saved through the Flood in the ark.

abraham.def: The patriarch called by JAH out of Ur of the Chaldees, father of the faithful, with whom God made the covenant of the Promised Land and a great posterity; father of Isaac.

abriham.def: A variant spelling of Abraham, the patriarch and father of the covenant people through Isaac.

isaac.def: The son of Abraham and Sarah, the child of promise whom Abraham was ready to offer to God; father of Jacob and Esau.

yis'haq.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Isaac, son of Abraham and Sarah and father of Jacob.

jacob.def: Son of Isaac and Rebekah, twin brother of Esau, renamed Israel by God; father of the twelve sons who became the twelve tribes of Israel.

ya`iqob.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Jacob (Ya'iqob), son of Isaac, renamed Israel, and father of the twelve tribes.

esau.def: The elder twin son of Isaac and Rebekah who sold his birthright to his brother Jacob; ancestor of the Edomites.

sara.def: Sarah, wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac; also, in the Book of Tobit, Sara the daughter of Raguel, freed from the demon Asmodeus to marry Tobias.

moses.def: The prophet who led Israel out of Egypt, parted the sea, and received the Law from JAH at Mount Sinai; the lawgiver and greatest prophet of Israel.

mussie.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Moses (Muse), the prophet who led Israel out of Egypt and received the Law at Sinai.

aaron.def: The elder brother of Moses and first high priest of Israel; spokesman before Pharaoh and head of the priestly line.

aron.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Aaron, brother of Moses and first high priest of Israel.

somson.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Samson, the Nazirite judge of Israel endowed with great strength, who fought the Philistines (Judges 13-16).

giediewon.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Gideon, the judge who delivered Israel from the Midianites with three hundred men (Judges 6-8).

deebora.def: Deborah, the prophetess and judge who, with the commander Barak, delivered Israel from the Canaanite king Jabin (Judges 4-5).

bariq.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Barak, the commander who with the prophetess Deborah defeated the Canaanite army of Sisera.

balaq.def: Balak, the king of Moab who hired the seer Balaam to curse Israel, only for the curses to become blessings (Numbers 22-24).

bele`am.def: Balaam, the pagan seer hired by Balak of Moab to curse Israel; God turned his curses into blessings, and his donkey spoke to him (Numbers 22-24).

qorie.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Korah, the Levite who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron and was swallowed by the earth (Numbers 16).

iyob.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Job, the righteous man of Uz whose faith endured great suffering and loss in the Book of Job.

samuel.def: The last judge and first great prophet of Israel, who anointed both Saul and David as king.

samu'iel.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Samuel, the prophet who anointed Saul and David as kings of Israel.

david.def: The shepherd-boy who slew Goliath and became the second and greatest king of Israel; psalmist and ancestor of the royal line and of the Messiah.

daweet.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of David (Dawit), the shepherd king of Israel, psalmist, and founder of the royal line.

gwolyad.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Goliath, the Philistine giant of Gath whom the young David killed with a sling and stone (1 Samuel 17).

solomon.def: The son of David and Bathsheba, king of Israel renowned for wisdom, who built the first Temple in Jerusalem.

selomon.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Solomon, David's son, the wise king who built the Temple.

asaph.def: A Levite appointed by David as a chief musician and singer in the Temple; several psalms bear his name.

elias.def: Elijah, the great prophet of the northern kingdom who confronted the prophets of Baal, called down fire from heaven, and was taken up in a whirlwind.

manasses.def: Manasseh — either the son of Joseph and his tribe, or King Manasseh of Judah known for wickedness and later repentance; also the name of Judith's late husband in the Book of Judith.

josias.def: Josiah, the righteous king of Judah who restored the Temple and renewed the covenant after finding the book of the Law (2 Kings 22-23).

hiziqyas.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Hezekiah, the faithful king of Judah delivered from the Assyrian Sennacherib and healed by God.

ezekias.def: Hezekiah (Greek form), the righteous king of Judah whom JAH delivered from Sennacherib's Assyrian army.

sennacherib.def: The king of Assyria who invaded Judah and besieged Jerusalem in Hezekiah's day, whose army was struck down by an angel (2 Kings 18-19); his death is noted in the Book of Tobit.

enemessar.def: Shalmaneser, the Assyrian king (as named in the Book of Tobit) who conquered the northern kingdom of Israel and carried the tribes, including Tobit, into captivity.

nabuchodonosor.def: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and the Temple and led Judah into exile. In the Book of Judith he is (unhistorically) called king of the Assyrians who sends Holofernes against Israel.

cyrus.def: Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian Empire, who conquered Babylon and issued the decree allowing the exiled Jews to return home and rebuild the Temple.

darius.def: Darius, king of Persia who confirmed the decree to rebuild the Temple; in 1 Esdras his contest of the three guardsmen leads to Zerubbabel's reward.

artexerxes.def: Artaxerxes, a king of Persia under whom the rebuilding of Jerusalem was for a time halted and later resumed, appearing in Ezra and 1 Esdras.

ptolemeus.def: Ptolemy, a Greek royal name (of the dynasty ruling Egypt after Alexander); appears in the superscription of the Greek Book of Esther.

pharaoh.def: The title of the kings of Egypt; in scripture especially the Pharaoh who oppressed Israel and resisted Moses before the Exodus.

fer`on.def: The Ge'ez/Amharic form of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt who enslaved Israel and was resisted by Moses.

iyasu.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of the name Joshua/Jesus (Iyasus). In context it usually renders Joshua, the successor of Moses who led Israel into Canaan, though the same name is the name of the Savior.

holofernes.def: The Assyrian general and commander-in-chief of Nebuchadnezzar's army in the Book of Judith, who besieged Bethulia. The widow Judith entered his camp and beheaded him as he lay drunk, breaking the siege.

judith.def: The devout and beautiful widow of Bethulia in the Book of Judith who, trusting in God, went into the Assyrian camp and beheaded the general Holofernes, delivering her people.

yodeet.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Judith, the widow of Bethulia who slew the Assyrian general Holofernes.

achior.def: The captain of the Ammonites in the Book of Judith who warned Holofernes that Israel could not be defeated while faithful to God; cast out to Bethulia, he later converted and joined Israel.

bagoas.def: The eunuch in charge of Holofernes' household in the Book of Judith, who discovered his master's beheaded body.

ozias.def: Ozias (Uzziah), one of the three ruling elders/governors of the town of Bethulia in the Book of Judith.

chabris.def: One of the three magistrates (with Ozias and Charmis) governing Bethulia in the Book of Judith.

charmis.def: One of the three magistrates (with Ozias and Chabris) governing Bethulia in the Book of Judith.

arphaxad.def: In the Book of Judith, the king of the Medes at Ecbatana whom Nebuchadnezzar defeats; also, in Genesis, a son of Shem in the line to Abraham.

tobit.def: The pious Israelite of the tribe of Naphtali, exiled to Nineveh, whose righteous deeds, blindness, and healing are told in the Book of Tobit that bears his name.

tobias.def: The son of Tobit in the Book of Tobit, who journeys with the angel Raphael (in disguise), marries Sara, drives off the demon Asmodeus, and heals his father's blindness.

anna.def: The wife of Tobit and mother of Tobias in the Book of Tobit.

raguel.def: The kinsman of Tobit living at Ecbatana in Media, father of Sara, who becomes the father-in-law of Tobias in the Book of Tobit. (Also the name of an archangel in the Book of Enoch.)

edna.def: The wife of Raguel and mother of Sara in the Book of Tobit.

gabael.def: The kinsman at Rages in Media with whom Tobit deposited ten talents of silver, later recovered by Tobias in the Book of Tobit.

achiacharus.def: Ahikar (Achiacharus), the nephew of Tobit and a high official at the Assyrian court in Nineveh, who provided for Tobit in his blindness.

esdras.def: Ezra, the priest and scribe who led a return of exiles and restored the Law in Jerusalem; the Books of Esdras (1 and 2 Esdras) bear his name and include his visions.

zorobabel.def: Zerubbabel, the Davidic prince who led the first return of exiles from Babylon and rebuilt the Temple; in 1 Esdras he wins Darius's favor by his speech on the strength of truth.

salathiel.def: Shealtiel, the father (or ancestor) of Zerubbabel in the Davidic line; also identified with Esdras in 2 Esdras.

jechonias.def: Jeconiah (Jehoiachin), the young king of Judah carried into Babylonian captivity; an ancestor of Zerubbabel.

josedec.def: Jozadak, the father of the high priest Jeshua (Joshua) who returned from exile with Zerubbabel to rebuild the Temple.

rathumus.def: A Persian officer (the 'story-writer' or chancellor) who wrote to Artaxerxes to halt the rebuilding of Jerusalem in 1 Esdras.

semellius.def: A Persian scribe who, with Rathumus, wrote to King Artaxerxes against the rebuilding of Jerusalem in 1 Esdras.

sisinnes.def: The governor of Syria and Phoenicia in 1 Esdras who inquired into the authority for rebuilding the Temple.

sathrabuzanes.def: A Persian official associated with Sisinnes in 1 Esdras who questioned the Jews' authority to rebuild the Temple.

bebai.def: The head of one of the families that returned from Babylonian exile, listed in Ezra/1 Esdras.

daniel.def: The prophet exiled to Babylon, famed for interpreting dreams, surviving the lions' den, and his visions; in the apocryphal additions he exposes the priests of Bel and slays the dragon, and rescues Susanna.

susanna.def: The virtuous wife falsely accused of adultery by two lecherous elders in the apocryphal addition to Daniel; the young Daniel proves her innocence by cross-examining the accusers.

bel.def: Bel (Marduk), the chief god of Babylon. In the apocryphal 'Bel and the Dragon,' Daniel exposes the fraud of Bel's priests who secretly ate the food offered to the idol.

chelcias.def: Helkias (Hilkiah), the father of Susanna in the apocryphal story of Susanna and the elders.

joacim.def: Joakim, the wealthy husband of Susanna in the apocryphal Susanna story; also a name of high priests in the apocrypha.

esther.def: The Jewish queen of Persia (also called Hadassah) who, at Mordecai's urging, risked her life to save her people from Haman's plot of genocide; the Book of Esther and its Greek additions tell her story.

astier.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Esther, the Jewish queen who saved her people from Haman in Persia.

mardocheus.def: Mordecai (Greek form), the Jewish courtier and cousin of Esther who raised her and uncovered a plot against the king, and whose refusal to bow provoked Haman's genocidal plan.

merdokyos.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Mordecai, the cousin of Esther who helped save the Jews from Haman.

aman.def: Haman, the chief minister of the Persian king in the Book of Esther who plotted to destroy all the Jews and was hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai.

jonas.def: Jonah, the prophet swallowed by the great fish and sent to preach repentance to Nineveh; cited in Tobit's prophecy of Nineveh's fall.

jeremy.def: Jeremiah, the prophet of Judah's last days who foretold the Babylonian exile; the apocryphal 'Epistle of Jeremy' warns the exiles against idolatry.

zacharias.def: Zechariah (Zacharias), a post-exilic prophet who encouraged the rebuilding of the Temple; the name is borne by several biblical figures.

aggeus.def: Haggai (Aggeus), the post-exilic prophet who urged Zerubbabel and the people to rebuild the Temple.

samaias.def: Shemaiah, a personal name borne by several figures in Ezra/1 Esdras, including priests and Levites of the return.

nathanael.def: Nethaneel, a personal name in the lists of Ezra/1 Esdras of those who had married foreign wives or served among the priests.

saraias.def: Seraiah, the name of the chief priest slain at the fall of Jerusalem and of other figures in Ezra/1 Esdras; an ancestor of Ezra.

zaraias.def: Zerahiah (or Zaraias), a name in the priestly genealogy of Ezra and among the returning exiles in 1 Esdras.

melchias.def: Malchijah (Melchias), a name borne by several men in the lists of Ezra/1 Esdras who had taken foreign wives.

azarias.def: Azariah — the name Raphael takes in disguise ('Azarias, son of Ananias') as Tobias's traveling companion in the Book of Tobit; also a common priestly name.

ananias.def: Hananiah (Ananias) — named as the kinsman of the disguised Raphael ('Azarias, son of Ananias') in Tobit, and elsewhere a common Hebrew name.

eleazar.def: Eleazar, a priestly name in scripture (the son of Aaron and later high priests); appears in the genealogies and histories of the apocrypha.

phinees.def: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron whose zeal turned away God's wrath, rewarded with a perpetual priesthood (Numbers 25); a name in priestly genealogies.

abiel.def: Abiel, an ancestor named in the genealogy of Tobit in the tribe of Naphtali.

tseerutsaydan.def: A figure named in the Ethiopic Books of Meqabyan. In these books such names belong to the kings and heroes of the Meqabyan narrative; the precise identity here is drawn from that Ethiopic tradition rather than the common Bible.

michael.def: The archangel Michael, chief of the holy angels and prince who defends Israel; in the Book of Enoch one of the four (or seven) archangels who intercede against the Watchers.

gabriel.def: The archangel Gabriel, one of the chief holy angels who stand before God; a messenger and, in Enoch, one of those set over the powers of heaven.

raphael.def: The archangel Raphael ('God heals'), who in the Book of Tobit travels disguised as 'Azarias' to guide Tobias, bind the demon Asmodeus, and heal Tobit's blindness; in Enoch he binds the Watcher Azazel.

uriel.def: The archangel Uriel ('fire/light of God'), who guides Enoch through the heavens and the courses of the luminaries in the Book of Enoch, and instructs Esdras in 2 Esdras.

phanuel.def: The archangel Phanuel, named in the Book of Enoch as one of the four angels of the presence, set over repentance and the hope of those who inherit eternal life.

keerubiel.def: A cherub-angel (the name means roughly 'cherub of God'), one of the exalted cherubim who attend the throne of JAH in the heavenly visions.

semjaza.def: In the Book of Enoch, the leader of the two hundred Watchers who descended on Mount Hermon; he led them in the oath to take human wives and so brought sin and ruin upon the earth.

azazel.def: In the Book of Enoch, one of the chief fallen Watchers who taught humanity to make weapons, cosmetics and sorcery; for his corruption he is bound and cast into darkness until the day of judgment. The name is linked to the scapegoat of Leviticus 16.

armaros.def: One of the fallen Watchers (chiefs of tens) in the Book of Enoch, who taught humankind the resolving of enchantments (the undoing of spells).

turel.def: One of the two hundred fallen Watchers listed among the leaders in the Book of Enoch.

deeyablos.def: The Devil — from the Greek 'Diabolos' ('slanderer, accuser'). The great adversary of JAH and of humankind, the deceiver who fell from heaven; equated with Satan.

seythan.def: Satan (Ge'ez/Amharic form), the adversary and accuser, the fallen angel who opposes JAH and tempts humanity to sin.

satan.def: The adversary and accuser, the fallen angel and prince of evil who opposes JAH and leads humanity into sin; identified with the Devil (Deeyablos).

leviathan.def: The great primeval sea-monster/dragon of the deep in scripture and Enoch; in the Book of Enoch the female Leviathan dwells in the abyss of the sea, kept for the day of judgment.

sa'ol.def: Sheol (Ge'ez/variant spelling), the abode of the dead beneath the earth, the shadowy grave-world where the departed await judgment.

see'ol.def: Sheol (variant spelling), the underworld abode of the dead in Hebrew thought, the grave and realm of departed souls.

sheol.def: The Hebrew abode of the dead beneath the earth, the grave-world where all the departed go to await the resurrection and judgment.

highest.def: 'The Highest' / the Most High — a title of JAH as the supreme God above all, especially frequent in Enoch and 2 Esdras.

almighty.def: A title of JAH as the all-powerful God (Hebrew El Shaddai), ruler over all creation.

saviour.def: A title of JAH as the deliverer and redeemer of His people, the one who saves from bondage, death and judgment.

maker.def: A title of JAH as the one who made all things; the Creator.

creator.def: A title of JAH as the maker of heaven, earth and all that is; rendered in Iyaric as 'Irator.'

pardoner.def: A title of JAH as the one who forgives and pardons sin; the merciful Redeemer.

elect.def: 'The Elect' / 'the Elect One' — in the Book of Enoch a title of the chosen Messiah/Son of Man, and also the 'elect' as the righteous chosen by JAH for salvation.

resurrection.def: The raising of the dead to life at the last day, when the righteous are rewarded and the wicked judged; a central hope of the apocrypha and of Rastafari faith in Iration and eternal life.

advent.def: The coming (or return) of the Messiah/JAH to judge the world and establish His kingdom; the awaited day of divine arrival.

parable.def: In the Book of Enoch, one of the 'Parables' (or Similitudes) — the three great visionary discourses (chapters 37-71) revealing the coming judgment, the Elect One/Son of Man, and the fate of the righteous and the wicked.

oreet.def: The Orit — the Ge'ez name for the Torah, specifically the Octateuch (the first eight books of the Bible) as received in Ethiopian tradition; the Law and its scriptures.

bible.def: The collected sacred scriptures. The Ethiopian Orthodox canon is notably broad, including books such as Enoch, Jubilees and the Meqabyan that other traditions treat as apocryphal.

testament.def: A 'covenant' between JAH and His people, and by extension the collections of scripture — the Old and New Testaments — recording those covenants.

septuagint.def: The ancient Greek translation of the Hebrew scriptures (traditionally by seventy scholars), which includes several of the apocryphal/deuterocanonical books used here.

masoretic.def: The Masoretic Text, the authoritative traditional Hebrew text of the Jewish scriptures, standardized by the Masoretes; often contrasted with the longer Greek Septuagint canon.

sirach.def: The Book of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus), a wisdom book of the apocrypha written by Jesus ben Sira, giving moral and practical teaching in the tradition of Proverbs.

ge'ez.def: Ge'ez (Ethiopic), the ancient classical language of Ethiopia and the liturgical and scriptural language of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, in which these apocrypha are preserved.

hebrew.def: The Hebrew language of the Israelites in which most of the Old Testament was written; also, the people and their scriptures.

greek.def: The Greek language in which the Septuagint and several apocryphal books survive; the tongue of the eastern Mediterranean in the Hellenistic era.

apocryphal.def: Describing the Apocrypha — books outside the shorter Hebrew canon but included in Greek, Ethiopic and other Bibles (such as Tobit, Judith, Esdras, and here Meqabyan and Enoch).

orthodox.def: Referring to the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church (and Eastern Orthodoxy generally), whose broad scriptural canon preserves these apocryphal books.

protestants.def: Protestant Christians, whose Bibles generally exclude the apocryphal/deuterocanonical books kept in the Orthodox and Catholic canons; referenced in the translation's editorial notes on canon.

protestant.def: Of the Protestant Christian tradition, whose canon omits the apocryphal books preserved by the Orthodox and Ethiopian churches.

christians.def: The followers of the Messiah; here referenced with respect to the differing biblical canons of Christian traditions.

adar.def: Adar, the twelfth month of the Hebrew calendar (February-March), in which the feast of Purim commemorates the deliverance of the Jews recounted in Esther.

ethiopia.def: The ancient African kingdom (Abyssinia / Kush), whose Orthodox Church preserves these scriptures; a land of deep significance in Rastafari faith as the promised homeland.

ityopphya.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Ethiopia, the African kingdom whose church preserves these books and which Rastafari revere as Zion on earth.

ethiopian.def: Of Ethiopia and its people; here especially the Ethiopian Orthodox tradition that preserves the Meqabyan and Enoch as scripture.

eritra.def: Eritrea, the region on the Red Sea coast north of Ethiopia (its name from the Greek 'Erythraean,' meaning Red); shares in the Ethiopic scriptural tradition. May also render the Erythraean (Red) Sea.

erythraean.def: The Erythraean Sea, the ancient Greek name for the Red Sea (and adjoining waters), 'the Red Sea.'

asia.def: Asia — in the apocrypha, the lands to the east; in Persian-period contexts, the provinces of the great eastern empires.

india.def: India, named as the easternmost bound of the Persian Empire (which stretched 'from India unto Ethiopia') in the Book of Esther.

hindekie.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of India, the far eastern limit of the Persian realm.

galilee.def: Galilee, the northern region of Israel around its lake; territory of the northern tribes, later the home region of Jesus.

samaria.def: Samaria, the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel and the surrounding region; later the land of the Samaritans.

semarya.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of Samaria, capital of the northern kingdom of Israel.

cilicia.def: Cilicia, a region on the southeastern coast of Asia Minor (modern Turkey), mentioned in the campaigns of the Book of Judith.

dothaim.def: Dothan (Dothaim), a town in the hills of northern Israel near the plain of Esdraelon, named in the Book of Judith as a point guarding the approach to Bethulia.

esdraelon.def: The great plain of Esdraelon (the Valley of Jezreel) in northern Israel, a strategic battlefield mentioned in the Book of Judith.

jordan.def: The Jordan River, the chief river of Israel flowing from Mount Hermon to the Dead Sea; Israel crossed it to enter the Promised Land.

yordanos.def: The Ge'ez (Ethiopic) form of the Jordan, the chief river of Israel.

seedona.def: Likely the Ge'ez form of Sidon, the ancient Phoenician port city on the Mediterranean coast north of Tyre. Identification is somewhat uncertain.

jesus.def: Jesus — in these apocryphal writings the name renders both Joshua/Jeshua (e.g. the high priest of the return) and, for Christian readers, the Messiah and Savior. Context determines which.

james.def: James — most likely a reference to the King James (Authorized) Version whose apocrypha these texts parallel, or to the apostle James. The reference here is editorial and its exact sense is uncertain.

keledans.def: A people named in the Ethiopic narrative; possibly a rendering of the Chaldeans or another nation. Identity uncertain.

iloflans.def: An Iyaric or Ge'ez-derived term in the translation whose reference is unclear; possibly a people or an 'I-word' coinage. Identity honestly uncertain.

iloflee.def: An Iyaric or dialect term in the translation whose meaning is not clearly determinable from the text. Honestly uncertain.

gielabuhie.def: A proper name (of a person or place) from the Ge'ez text whose biblical identity is uncertain.

gibts.def: A dialect/Iyaric term in the translation; possibly a rendering of 'Egypt' (Copt/Gypt) or a patois form. Meaning honestly uncertain.

abya.def: A proper name from the Ethiopic text (possibly Abijah or a Meqabyan figure); exact identity uncertain.

seela.def: A proper name from the Ethiopic text whose biblical identity is uncertain.

fentos.def: A proper name from the Ethiopic text whose reference is uncertain; possibly a place or a figure in the Meqabyan narrative.

riemat.def: A proper name from the Ethiopic text whose identity is uncertain.

siefor.def: A proper name from the Ethiopic text; possibly a rendering of Zipporah or Zephar. Identity uncertain.

seena.def: A place name in the Ethiopic text; possibly Sinai or Zion (Seyon). Identification uncertain.

shekina.def: The Shekinah is the indwelling Presence or manifest Glory of God, the aspect of the divine that dwells among creatures and rests upon the Throne of Glory. In 3 Enoch it fills the highest heaven of Araboth and is the radiance in whose light the angelic hosts stand.

throne of glory.def: The celestial Throne (kisse ha-kavod) on which the divine Glory is enthroned, the central object of Merkabah mysticism. In 3 Enoch it stands in the highest heaven Araboth, borne and surrounded by the Chayyoth, Ophannim, Cherubim and Seraphim.

raqia.def: The firmament or expanse of heaven (Hebrew raqia, from Genesis 1), the solid vault stretched across the cosmos. In 3 Enoch each of the seven heavens is a raqia, the highest being the Araboth Raqia where the Throne of Glory rests.

araboth.def: Araboth (Aravot) is the seventh and highest of the heavens in 3 Enoch and rabbinic cosmology, the dwelling place of the Throne of Glory, the Shekinah, and the highest ranks of angels. Its name derives from Psalm 68:4, 'him who rides upon the Aravot.'

metatron.def: The supreme angel of 3 Enoch (the Sefer Hekhalot), styled the 'lesser YHWH' and Prince of the Presence, who is the patriarch Enoch translated and transformed into a fiery archangel. He is enthroned as vice-regent over the heavenly household and reveals its secrets to Rabbi Ishmael.

merkaba.def: The Merkabah is the divine Throne-Chariot of God derived from Ezekiel's vision (Ezekiel 1), the supreme object of Hekhalot and Merkabah mysticism. Contemplation of and ascent to the Merkabah is the central concern of 3 Enoch.

chayyoth.def: The Chayyoth (Chayot ha-Qodesh, 'holy living creatures') are the four-faced, four-winged beings of Ezekiel 1 that bear and stand beneath the Throne of Glory. In 3 Enoch they form the highest angelic order, their prince being Chayyliel.

seraphim.def: The 'burning ones' of Isaiah 6, a fiery angelic order with six wings who stand about the Throne crying 'Holy, holy, holy.' In 3 Enoch they attend the Merkabah under their prince Seraphiel.

kerubim.def: The Cherubim, an exalted angelic order associated with the Throne and the divine chariot, bearing and guarding the Glory. In 3 Enoch they stand about the Merkabah under their prince Kerubiel.

ophannim.def: The Ophannim ('wheels') are an angelic order derived from the whirling wheels beside the Chayyoth in Ezekiel 1, ranked among the highest attendants of the Throne. In 3 Enoch their prince is Ophanniel.

maqom.def: Ha-Maqom, 'the Place,' a rabbinic and Hekhalot circumlocution for God as the omnipresent one who is the place of the world while the world is not his place. It appears in 3 Enoch as a reverential name for the Deity.

dan.def: One of the tribes and territories of Israel (also a city in the far north); it appears in the geographic and tribal references of the Enochic material.

divine presence.def: The Shekinah, the manifest Presence of God that dwells upon the Throne of Glory. The great angel Metatron bears the title 'Prince of the Presence' (Sar ha-Panim) as the one who ministers before it.

presence.def: The divine Presence (the Shekinah/Panim) before which the highest angels minister; Metatron is the Sar ha-Panim, the Prince of the Presence, in 3 Enoch.

yhwh.def: The Tetragrammaton, the ineffable four-letter proper name of God (YHWH). In 3 Enoch, Metatron is called the 'lesser YHWH' because the divine Name was placed upon him.

eden.def: The Garden of Eden, the paradise of Genesis; in the Enochic and Hekhalot traditions it is the abode of the righteous dead and the tree of life, sometimes located in the third heaven (2 Enoch).

majesty.def: A reverential title for God as the enthroned Glory ('the Great Majesty' or 'the Majesty and Glory' in 1 Enoch), before whom the angelic hosts cannot draw near.

prince.def: In 3 Enoch a 'prince' (sar) is a ruling angel set over a heaven, an element, a nation, or an angelic host; Metatron is the chief of these, the Prince of the Presence.

keepers.def: Guardian angels who keep watch, in 3 Enoch stationed as keepers or wardens at the gates and halls of the heavenly palaces (Hekhalot).

tora.def: The Torah, the divine Law and teaching revealed to Israel; in the Hekhalot tradition of 3 Enoch it is a preexistent heavenly reality studied and guarded in the celestial academy.

sopheriel.def: In 3 Enoch, Sopheriel is the name of two great angel-princes, Sopheriel YHWH the Killer (MeMit) and Sopheriel YHWH the Lifegiver (Mehayye), who keep the books of the dead and the living before the Throne.

qaddishin.def: The Qaddishin ('holy ones') are, with the Irin ('watchers'), an exalted class of angelic princes in 3 Enoch who sit in the heavenly court of judgment before the Holy One (cf. Daniel 4).

angel.def: A messenger and servant of God; the Enochic and Hekhalot texts describe vast hierarchies of angels ordered around the Throne, each with appointed offices, names, and hosts.

paradise.def: The heavenly garden of the righteous (paradise/Eden); in 2 Enoch it is located in the third heaven and prepared as the eternal inheritance of the just, while its opposite quarter holds the place of punishment.

enosh.def: The son of Seth and grandson of Adam (Genesis 5), of whom it was said that in his day men began to call on the name of the LORD; an early figure in the antediluvian genealogy.

vretil.def: In 2 Enoch, Vretil (Vrevoil) is the swiftest of the archangels and the heavenly scribe who brings out the books and dictates to Enoch the knowledge of all creation, which Enoch records in 360-odd books.

semj.def: Semjaza (Shemihazah), the chief leader of the two hundred Watchers who in 1 Enoch 6 bind themselves by oath on Mount Hermon to descend and take human wives; a principal instigator of the angelic fall.

messiah.def: The Anointed One; in the Parables of 1 Enoch the messianic figure ('his Anointed') is bound up with the Elect One and the Son of Man who executes the final judgment.

ishmael.def: Rabbi Ishmael ben Elisha, the priest and Tannaitic sage who is the human protagonist of 3 Enoch: he ascends to the heavens, is received by Metatron, and receives from him the revelation of the celestial world.

kerub.def: A cherub, a single member of the Cherubim, the exalted throne-bearing order of angels associated with the Merkabah.

wheels.def: The Ophannim, the whirling wheels beside the living creatures in Ezekiel's vision, reckoned in 3 Enoch as an angelic order attending the Throne.

lesser.def: In 3 Enoch, 'the lesser YHWH' is the title given to Metatron, the exalted angel upon whom God set his own Name (cf. Exodus 23:21, 'my name is in him').

shamayim.def: Shamayim, 'the heavens,' the Hebrew term for the sky and the heavenly realm; in 3 Enoch it names one of the seven heavens through which the ascent proceeds.

irin.def: The Irin ('watchers') are, with the Qaddishin ('holy ones'), the exalted angel-princes of the heavenly court of judgment in 3 Enoch (cf. the 'watcher, a holy one' of Daniel 4). Distinct from the fallen Watchers of 1 Enoch.

nehar.def: Part of the phrase Nehar di-Nur, the 'river of fire' (Daniel 7:10) that flows out from before the Throne of Glory in 3 Enoch, from which the ministering angels are formed and into which they are consumed.

nur.def: Nur, 'fire' (Aramaic), the element of the Nehar di-Nur, the river of fire streaming from beneath the Throne of Glory in the Hekhalot visions of 3 Enoch.

yah.def: A short form of the Tetragrammaton (Yah), used in doxologies and embedded in angelic and divine names.

tsivan.def: In 2 Enoch, a name given to one of the highest heavens or heavenly regions near the Throne, part of the sequence of heavens Enoch traverses.

eve.def: The first woman, wife of Adam and mother of humankind (Genesis 2-4), named in the primeval history that frames the Enochic genealogies.

amram.def: The father of Moses, Aaron and Miriam (Exodus 6); a figure of the Levitical line named in the ancestral traditions.

qedushsha.def: The Qedushshah ('sanctification'), the angelic and liturgical proclamation of God's holiness ('Holy, holy, holy,' Isaiah 6) sung before the Throne; in 3 Enoch the heavenly hosts recite it in their appointed order.

anaphiel.def: Anaphiel YHWH is one of the greatest angel-princes of 3 Enoch, keeper of the seal and warden of the highest halls, so exalted that he is set over the other princes; it is he who bears Enoch/Metatron. His name is linked to anaph, 'bough/branch.'

galgallim.def: The Galgallim ('spheres' or 'wheels,' galgal) are an angelic order of the Merkabah in 3 Enoch, akin to the Ophannim, associated with the whirling wheels of the divine chariot; their prince is Rikbiel.

mikael.def: Michael (Mikael), the great archangel and prince of Israel, chief of the ministering angels who serves before the Throne in 3 Enoch.

zebul.def: Zebul ('lofty abode') is, in 3 Enoch and rabbinic cosmology, one of the seven heavens, the heaven in which the heavenly Jerusalem, Temple and altar stand and where the prince Michael offers sacrifice.

rahatiel.def: In 3 Enoch, Rahatiel is the angel-prince set over the constellations (the mazzaloth), who leads the stars in their courses; his name is linked to the root for 'running/coursing.'

shechaqim.def: Shechaqim ('clouds/skies') is one of the seven heavens in 3 Enoch and rabbinic cosmology, the heaven in which the millstones grind manna for the righteous.

gehenna.def: Gehenna (Gehinnom), the place of fiery punishment for the wicked, named from the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem. In the Enochic and Hekhalot tradition it is the abode of judgment set opposite paradise.

joshua.def: The successor of Moses who led Israel into the promised land; named among the transmitters of the tradition and the righteous of Israel.

grigori.def: The Grigori (Greek 'watchers') are, in 2 Enoch, the order of Watchers, some of whom fell with their prince Satanail; Enoch finds a company of them mourning in the fifth heaven and exhorts them to resume their liturgy.

methosalem.def: A form of the name Methuselah (Methosalam), son of Enoch, prominent in 2 Enoch where Enoch instructs him and his brethren before his final ascent.

sari.def: Sariel (also Suriel), one of the archangels of 1 Enoch, 'set over the spirits' and named among the holy ones who watch over humankind; the truncated token here stands for his name.

enos.def: Enosh, son of Seth and grandson of Adam (Genesis 5), an early patriarch in the antediluvian line.

seth.def: The third son of Adam and Eve, appointed in place of Abel, and ancestor of the righteous line leading to Enoch and Noah (Genesis 4-5).

satans.def: In the Parables of 1 Enoch, the 'satans' are a class of accusing and tempting angelic beings who dwell in judgment and lead humanity astray, distinct from the ordinary hosts of heaven.

anointed.def: The Anointed One (Messiah); in the Parables of 1 Enoch 'his Anointed' is the eschatological figure associated with the Elect One and the Son of Man.

behemoth.def: The great land-monster of primeval creation; in 1 Enoch 60 Behemoth is the male beast set in the desert (Dendain), paired with Leviathan, reserved for the eschatological banquet of the righteous.

cherubin.def: The Cherubim, the throne-bearing angelic order associated with the Merkabah; a variant spelling used in the Enochic material.

seraphin.def: The Seraphim, the fiery six-winged angels of Isaiah 6 who surround the Throne; a variant spelling in the Enochic material.

ophannin.def: The Ophannim, the 'wheels' of the Merkabah reckoned as an angelic order; a variant spelling in the Enochic material.

hel.def: In 2 Enoch (Slavonic), a name of the place of darkness and punishment for the wicked, the infernal region shown to Enoch on his heavenly journey.

servant.def: A title of honor for the righteous one who serves God; in the Parables tradition it overlaps with the Elect One and the Son of Man as the chosen agent of divine purpose.

dibbur.def: Dibbur, the divine 'Word' or 'utterance'; in the Hekhalot idiom the creative and commanding speech that proceeds from God, associated with the giving of the commandments.

flood.def: The Deluge of Genesis 6-9, the cosmic judgment by water brought on because of the corruption of the Watchers and the giants; a central event of the Enochic history from which Noah is saved.

crown.def: The celestial crown (kether); in 3 Enoch a crown of glory is set upon Metatron's head, and the angels and the righteous are adorned with crowns of light before the Throne.

acher.def: Acher ('the Other'), the byname of Elisha ben Abuyah, the sage who in the Hekhalot tradition ascended to the Merkabah, saw Metatron enthroned, and fell into the heresy of 'two powers in heaven'; his story is told in 3 Enoch 16.

gabriel_prince.def: Gabriel, the archangel 'set over the garden and the cherubim' in 1 Enoch, who in 3 Enoch is a great prince ministering before the Throne. (Capitalized GABRIEL in the source marks this angelic sense.)

bad.def: In 3 Enoch, part of the name of an angel-prince (the source token BAD standing for a compound theophoric name such as Baradiel or a like prince set over an element); an angelic office of the celestial hierarchy.

ariel.def: Ariel ('lion of God' or 'hearth of God') is an angelic name; in the Hekhalot and related traditions an angel-prince, the name also being an epithet applied to the altar and to Jerusalem (Isaiah 29).

makon.def: Makon ('foundation/fixed place') is one of the seven heavens in 3 Enoch and rabbinic cosmology, the heaven that stores the treasuries of snow, hail, dew and the storehouses of blessing.

sother.def: In 3 Enoch, a name associated with the angelic guardians/scribes of the heavenly household; the source preserves it among the many named princes whose exact office is uncertain.

ashiel.def: One of the '-el' angel-princes named in 3 Enoch's catalogues of the celestial hierarchy; its precise office is not clearly specified in the text and remains uncertain.

rikbiel.def: In 3 Enoch, Rikbiel YHWH is the great prince set over the wheels of the Merkabah (the Galgallim), who governs the divine Chariot; his name derives from rekhev, 'chariot.'

chayya.def: Chayya (singular of Chayyoth), a single one of the holy living creatures that bear the Throne in the Merkabah vision of 3 Enoch.

chayyliel.def: In 3 Enoch, Chayyliel YHWH is the mighty angel-prince set over the Chayyoth (the living creatures); a single glance of him is said to be able to swallow up the ministering angels.

kerubiel.def: In 3 Enoch, Kerubiel YHWH is the angel-prince set over the Cherubim, a being of fire, lightning and immense stature who governs the throne-bearing cherubic host.

ribbotaim.def: Ribbotaim ('myriads upon myriads'), a term of numberless multitude used in 3 Enoch for the vast hosts of the chariots and angels of the Merkabah (cf. Psalm 68:17).

ophphanniel.def: In 3 Enoch, Ophanniel YHWH is the great angel-prince set over the Ophannim (the wheels), described with many faces, wings and eyes, who guards and turns the wheels of the Merkabah.

seraphiel.def: In 3 Enoch, Seraphiel YHWH is the towering fiery angel-prince set over the Seraphim, whose body is of glowing coals and who leads the seraphic host in the thrice-holy Qedushshah.

radweriel.def: In 3 Enoch, Radweriel YHWH is the angel-prince and heavenly archivist, keeper of the scroll-cases and the Book of Records, from whose mouth new songs of praise and companies of angels come forth.

ehye.def: Ehyeh ('I AM,' from 'Ehyeh asher Ehyeh,' Exodus 3:14), a divine name of God's self-existence used reverentially in the Hekhalot invocations of 3 Enoch.

zaaphiel.def: In 3 Enoch, Za'aphiel (Zaapiel) is an angel-prince of wrath or storm, one of the officers of the celestial court; his name is linked to za'aph, 'rage/storm.'

simkiel.def: In 3 Enoch, Simkiel is one of the angels of destruction/mercy set over the punishment and refinement of souls in the intermediate state; an officer of the heavenly judgment.

curtain.def: The Pargod, the cosmic curtain or veil spread before the Throne of Glory in 3 Enoch, on which all the generations and events of history are woven and from behind which the divine decrees issue.

joseph.def: The son of Jacob who rose to power in Egypt; a patriarch named among the righteous ancestors of Israel in the tradition.

yehoel.def: Yahoel (Yehoel), an exalted angel who bears the divine Name within him; named in 3 Enoch among the seventy names of Metatron and known from the Apocalypse of Abraham as the angel who guides the patriarch.

whyh.def: A permuted writing of the Tetragrammaton (the letters of YHWH reordered), used in the Hekhalot and Enochic magical-liturgical tradition as a holy Name of power.

beyah.def: 'Be-Yah,' meaning 'in Yah/by the LORD' (cf. Isaiah 26:4), taken in the mystical tradition as a divine Name and marker of God's power in creation.

halakas.def: Halakhot, the legal rulings and traditions of rabbinic law; named in 3 Enoch among the bodies of sacred learning (with Haggadot, Toseftot, etc.) that Metatron reveals or that are studied in the heavenly academy.

haggadas.def: Haggadot, the non-legal, narrative and homiletical teachings of the rabbis; listed in 3 Enoch among the branches of Torah knowledge revealed in heaven.

toseftas.def: Toseftot, the supplementary rabbinic traditions and additions to the Mishnah; named in 3 Enoch among the categories of sacred learning.

synagogue.def: The Great Synagogue (Keneset ha-Gedolah), the body of early sages to whom tradition was transmitted; named in the chain of transmission behind the Hekhalot teaching.

ezra.def: The scribe and priest who restored the Law after the exile; named among the transmitters and expounders of the Torah in the tradition.

hillel.def: The great Tannaitic sage Hillel the Elder, head of one of the two chief schools of early rabbinic law; named among the authorities of the tradition.

abbahu.def: Rabbi Abbahu, a prominent Palestinian Amora (3rd-4th c.); cited among the rabbinic authorities associated with the transmission of the teaching.

zera.def: Rabbi Zera (Ze'ira), a Palestinian-Babylonian Amora; named among the sages in the rabbinic framework surrounding the Hekhalot material.

methusal.def: A shortened form of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, addressed in the closing testamentary chapters of the Enochic literature.

regim.def: In 2 Enoch, one of the men (with Riman/Gaidad) who attend Enoch or witness his ascent and return; a name from the Slavonic narrative frame.

gaidal.def: In 2 Enoch (Slavonic), one of the companions or sons associated with Enoch's departure and the instruction of his household.

satanail.def: In 2 Enoch, Satanail is the prince of the Grigori (Watchers) who conceived the impossible thought of setting his throne above the clouds to be equal to God, and was cast down with his angels; the arch-rebel of the Slavonic Enoch.

sabaoth.def: '(Lord of) Sabaoth,' meaning 'of hosts' (tseva'ot), the title of God as Lord of the heavenly armies, used in the doxologies of the Enochic and Hekhalot traditions.

adoil.def: In 2 Enoch's cosmogony, Adoil is the great primeval light/aeon whom God summons before creation; when Adoil bursts apart, the visible light and the foundation of all things (the 'great age') come forth.

arkhas.def: In 2 Enoch's cosmogony, Arkhas (Arukhas) is the primeval dark entity summoned by God after Adoil; from his dissolution comes the lower, dark foundation of the created order, counterpart to the light of Adoil.

zodiac.def: The belt of twelve constellations through which the sun and planets move; the astronomical portions of 1 and 2 Enoch describe the sun's course through its heavenly gates and the ordering of the signs.

thevan.def: In 2 Enoch, a name given to one of the heavenly regions or the movements of the luminaries in the astronomical revelation shown to Enoch.

achuzan.def: In 2 Enoch, Achuzan is the name for the sacred central place of the earth (identified with the site of Jerusalem/the Temple mount), the 'navel' where Enoch's descendants are to worship.

kesbeel.def: In 1 Enoch 69, Kesbeel (Kasbeel) is the fallen angel who obtains and misuses the knowledge of the hidden Oath and the secret Name (the Akae), by which heaven and earth are held together.

dudael.def: In 1 Enoch 10, Dudael is the desert place of jagged rocks into which the archangel Raphael casts the bound Azazel, to lie in darkness until the final judgment by fire.

elect one.def: In the Parables of 1 Enoch, the Elect One (Chosen One) is the preexistent heavenly redeemer, identified with the Son of Man, who is seated on the throne of glory by the Lord of Spirits to judge the kings and the mighty and to vindicate the righteous.

son of man.def: In the Parables of 1 Enoch, the Son of Man is a heavenly, preexistent figure (identified with the Elect One and the Anointed) revealed before the Lord of Spirits, who sits on the throne of glory to execute judgment; at the close of the work he is identified with Enoch himself.

lord of spirits.def: The characteristic title of God in the Parables of 1 Enoch, 'the Lord of Spirits,' the sovereign of the heavenly hosts before whom the Elect One is enthroned and by whose name the righteous are vindicated.

ancient of days.def: The title of God as the aged, enthroned Judge (from Daniel 7), 'the Head of Days' in 1 Enoch, before whom the Son of Man is presented and the books of judgment are opened.

head of days.def: In the Parables of 1 Enoch, the 'Head (Antecedent) of Days' is God enthroned as the primeval Judge, equivalent to Daniel's Ancient of Days, whose head is white like wool and before whom the Son of Man appears.

sariel.def: One of the archangels of 1 Enoch (also Suriel), reckoned among the holy watchers set over the spirits of humankind; in some lists one of the four or seven who bring the giants' outcry before God.

remiel.def: One of the seven archangels of 1 Enoch 20 (Ramiel), 'whom God set over those who rise,' an angel associated with the resurrection and with true visions. His name means 'thunder of God' or 'God raises up.'

wisdom.def: In the Parables of 1 Enoch (chapter 42) Wisdom is personified as a heavenly being who went out to dwell among humankind, found no dwelling place, and returned to take her seat among the angels; a hypostasis of the divine ordering of creation.

venus.def: The morning/evening star, one of the wandering luminaries whose courses and gates are described in the astronomical portions of 1 and 2 Enoch attributed to the guidance of the archangel Uriel.

din.def: Din, 'judgment/law'; part of the phrase Beth Din, the celestial court of justice in which the angel-princes (the Irin and Qaddishin) sit before the Throne to render the divine verdicts in 3 Enoch.

beth din.def: The Beth Din ha-Gadol, the great heavenly court of judgment in 3 Enoch, where the angelic princes assemble before the Throne of Glory and the books of the living and the dead are opened for the divine decree.

a'ah.def: A permutation of the Divine Name — a letter-combination of the Tetragrammaton/Ehyeh used in the Hekhalot letter-mysticism of Sefer Hekhalot. Such Name-forms cluster in 3 Enoch's accounts of the crowns, seals, and adjurations, where the powers of the Divine Name are spoken over the Merkabah; the individual form is esoteric and not independently translated.

adrigon.def: One of the seventy names of Metatron / the great seal-names listed in Sefer Hekhalot (3 Enoch, esp. ch. 48D), by which the Prince of the Presence is invoked and sealed; the exact meaning of the individual name is esoteric.

akatriel.def: 'Crown of God': the first element of the full divine name Akatriel Yah Yehod Sebaoth, denoting the crowned Glory enthroned on the Merkabah; sometimes treated as a great crowning angel/name of the Presence.

akatriel yah yehod sebaoth.def: A full name of the enthroned Glory of God in the Hekhalot texts (3 Enoch 15B), the King crowned upon the throne of the Merkabah whom R. Ishmael beheld. It combines Akatriel ('crown of God') with Yah, Yehod, and Sebaoth ('of hosts').

aniyel.def: Aniyel (Aniel) YHWH, a prince who stands as a keeper at the gate of one of the heavenly halls among the guardian princes (3 Enoch 18).

aph'apiel.def: A spelling of Aphaphiel, an angelic prince of the Hekhalot lists whose office is uncertain.

aphaphiel.def: Aphaphiel (Aph-Aphiel), one of the angelic princes named in the Hekhalot lists; his office is not clearly specified.

araphiel.def: Araphiel YHWH, one of the great princes named among the guardians of the halls of Araboth (3 Enoch 18).

arinkh.def: Ariukh (Arioch), one of the two angels whom God appoints in 2 Enoch to guard Enoch's writings and preserve them for later generations.

asum.def: One of the seventy names of Metatron / the great seal-names listed in Sefer Hekhalot (3 Enoch, esp. ch. 48D), by which the Prince of the Presence is invoked and sealed; the exact meaning of the individual name is esoteric.

atrugiel.def: Atrugiel (Atrugniel), a great prince of the Presence named among the exalted princes who stand over the heavenly host (3 Enoch 18).

azbuga.def: Azbuga(h) YHWH, one of the eight great princes of the Presence, who girds the righteous with garments of life and clothes them for the world to come (3 Enoch 18).

azbuga-yhwh.def: See Azbuga: one of the eight princes who clothe the righteous.

azza.def: Azza (Uzza), one of the angels who objected to Enoch's exaltation as Metatron; a fallen Watcher-prince cast down for opposing God's decree and for the corruption of the generation of the Flood (3 Enoch 4; 5).

azzael.def: Azzael (Azael/Aza'el), one of the objecting/fallen angels associated with Azza and Uzza, reckoned among the Watchers who descended and taught forbidden arts (3 Enoch 4; 5).

azziel.def: Azziel (Uzziel), one of the fallen/objecting angels grouped with Azza and Azzael among the Watchers who resisted Enoch's elevation (3 Enoch 4; 5).

bakariel.def: Bakariel, one of the angelic princes named in the Hekhalot lists of 3 Enoch; his particular office is not specified in the sources.

baradiel.def: Baradiel, the prince set over hail (barad), one of the cosmic princes governing the weather (3 Enoch 14; 17).

barakiel.def: Barakiel, a spelling of Baraqiel, prince over lightning (baraq).

baraq.def: 'Lightning' (baraq), one of the natural powers governed by the weather-princes (its prince being Baraqiel) in the cosmology of 3 Enoch.

baraqiel.def: Baraqiel, the prince set over lightning (baraq) among the princes of the natural powers (3 Enoch 14).

barattiel.def: Barattiel, a mighty prince who upholds the highest heaven (Araboth) upon the tips of his three fingers (3 Enoch 18).

chalkadri.def: Variant of Chalkydri, the sun-birds of 2 Enoch that fly before the sun and burst into song as it rises.

chalkidri.def: The Chalkydri, brazen serpent-birds (part-lion, part-crocodile) of the sun described in 2 Enoch, who accompany the sun's chariot and sing at its rising; wondrous flying elements of the fourth heaven.

chashmal.def: The 'electrum / amber' radiance seen in Ezekiel 1:4,27, the glowing brilliance at the heart of the Merkabah vision; also the source-name of the Chashmallim angelic order.

chashmallim.def: The order of the Chashmallim, angels of the electrum-radiance (chashmal) of Ezekiel 1; one of the great angelic ranks of the Merkabah.

chashmattim.def: A transmitted/variant form of the Chashmallim, the angels of the electrum-radiance (chashmal) of the Merkabah.

chayyot.def: The Chayyoth (Chayyot ha-Qodesh), the 'living creatures' of Ezekiel's vision who bear the throne of Glory; the highest order under the Merkabah, set over by the prince Chayyliel.

degalim.def: 'Banners / divisions', the standard-bearing companies into which the angelic host is divided, each under its banner.

dibburiel.def: Dibburiel, a prince named among the guardians of the gates of the heavenly halls; his exact office is not detailed beyond his rank among the hall-princes.

dubbiel.def: Dubbiel ('bear of God'), the guardian prince of the kingdom of Persia, who for a time supplanted Israel's advocate before the throne (3 Enoch 26).

e'eseh.def: The self-naming of God 'Ehyeh' ('I AM / I WILL BE', Exodus 3:14), counted among the great Names in the Hekhalot mysticism of the Divine Name.

el-shaddai.def: 'God Almighty', a biblical name of God invoked in the Enoch traditions among the powers and seals of the Divine Name.

elim.def: 'Gods / mighty ones', one of the exalted classes of angels named in 3 Enoch 14:1 who tremble before Metatron's crown.

er'ellim.def: 'The valiant ones', an angelic order (from Isaiah 33:7) listed among the ranks that fear before the crown of Metatron in 3 Enoch 14:1.

erellim.def: 'The valiant ones' (Er'ellim), an angelic order (from Isaiah 33:7) named among the ranks trembling before Metatron's crown in 3 Enoch 14:1.

ermon.def: Mount Hermon (Ermon), the mountain on which, in the Enoch traditions, the Watchers/Grigori descended and bound themselves by oath to their transgression.

galgalliel.def: Galgalliel YHWH, the prince set over the orb/wheel of the sun, with seventy-two angels under him driving the sun through the sky (3 Enoch 14; 17).

gallisur.def: Gallisur (Galisur/Galsur, identified with Raziel), the prince who reveals the reasons of the Torah and proclaims the decrees issued from behind the heavenly curtain.

gebura.def: 'Geburah', the divine Might/Power; also used as a reverent circumlocution for God (as 'the Power') in rabbinic-Hekhalot idiom.

geburatiel.def: Geburatiel YHWH, the prince set over strength/might (geburah), one of the princes who guard the entrances of the heavenly halls (3 Enoch 18).

gedudim.def: 'Troops / legions' (gedudim), bands of the angelic army arrayed in the heavens under their banners.

gibborim.def: 'Mighty ones / warriors', the valiant angels of the heavenly host.

ha-shshamayim.def: 'The heavens' (ha-shamayim), the general term for the heavenly expanse spanning the seven graded firmaments.

kainan.def: Kenan (Kainan) son of Enosh, one of the antediluvian patriarchs of the line of Seth in the genealogy of Genesis 5.

khermion.def: A transmitted spelling associated with Mount Hermon, the place linked with the descent of the Watchers/Grigori in the Enoch traditions.

kokbiel.def: Kokbiel (Kokabiel), the prince set over the stars (kokhavim), marshalling the host of the fixed stars (3 Enoch 17).

lailiel.def: Lailiel, the prince set over the night (laylah), one of the princes governing the times (3 Enoch 14).

ma'on.def: Ma'on, the fifth of the seven heavens, where companies of ministering angels sing by night and are silent by day for the sake of Israel's praise.

mal'akim.def: 'Messengers / angels' (mal'akhim), the general term for the angelic beings who serve God and bear his word.

malaleel.def: Mahalalel (Malaleel) son of Kenan, an antediluvian patriarch in the Sethite genealogy of Genesis 5.

margeziel.def: Margeziel, one of the princes of the heavenly halls named in the Hekhalot lists; office uncertain.

matariel.def: Matariel, the prince set over rain (matar), governing the waters that fall on the earth (3 Enoch 14).

mathusal.def: Methuselah (Mathusal) son of Enoch, the longest-lived of the patriarchs (Genesis 5:27); in the Enoch traditions the recipient of Enoch's parting instruction.

merkabah.def: The 'Chariot'-throne of God (Ezekiel 1), the central object of Hekhalot vision; Sefer Hekhalot is a supreme example of Merkabah mysticism.

mesharetim.def: 'Ministers', the ministering angels (mal'akhei ha-sharet) who serve before the throne.

methusalem.def: A Greek/Slavonic form of Methuselah, son of Enoch, addressed by Enoch in the farewell discourses of 2 Enoch.

mirjam.def: Mirjam (Miriam), a personal name occurring in the transmitted Enoch material; a Hebrew name borne notably by the sister of Moses.

mottron.def: A manuscript/OCR variant of the name Metatron, the transformed Enoch and Prince of the Presence.

na'ar.def: 'Youth' (Na'ar), a standing epithet of Metatron in 3 Enoch, expressing that though the greatest of the princes he is 'young' among the primordial powers; the ministering angels call him by this name.

na'aririel.def: Na'aririel YHWH, one of the great princes of Araboth named in the ascending order of honour among the highest princes (3 Enoch 18).

neganzegael.def: Neganzegael, an angel-name appearing among the princes/powers named in the transmitted Enoch material; its precise office is not clearly established in the sources and should be treated as uncertain.

ophanniel.def: Ophanniel YHWH, the prince set over the Ophannim (wheels), watching over their many eyes and their ceaseless whirling (3 Enoch 25).

ophanniel-yhwh.def: See Ophanniel: the prince set over the Ophannim of the Merkabah.

paaziel.def: Pa'aziel, a prince named among the guardians of the gates of the heavenly halls; his precise office is not detailed.

pachriel.def: Pachriel, a guardian prince of the heavenly halls named in the Hekhalot lists; his specific function is not clearly specified in the sources.

parashim.def: 'Horsemen', a martial rank among the heavenly hosts.

pargod.def: The Pargod, the cosmic curtain/veil hung before the throne of Glory, on which past and future are woven and behind which the deepest secrets are hidden.

parinkh.def: Pariukh (Marioch), the second of the two angels appointed in 2 Enoch to guard Enoch's writings alongside Arioch.

paspasiel.def: Paspasiel, one of the princes stationed at the gates of the heavenly halls in the Hekhalot lists; office not further specified.

pazriel.def: Pazriel, a prince named among the guardians of the heavenly gates in the Hekhalot lists; his office is uncertain.

pisqon.def: Pisqon, one of the seventy names of Metatron in 3 Enoch 48D, traditionally explained as 'he who suspends/decides' (poseq), a title of the Prince of the Presence.

qafsiel.def: Qafsiel (Qaphsiel/Kafziel), a prince associated in the traditions with the moon or the planet Saturn; his precise office in the lists is variously reported.

qinoth.def: 'Qinoth', dirges/lamentations; in the heavenly liturgy the mournful strains raised over the exile of the Shekhinah and Israel's suffering.

ra'amiel.def: Ra'amiel, the prince set over thunder (ra'am) among the princes of the storm (3 Enoch 14).

ra'ashiel.def: Ra'ashiel, the prince set over earthquake/quaking (ra'ash), causing the trembling of the earth (3 Enoch 14).

rabibiel.def: Rabibiel, a prince whose name is linked to the rains/showers (rebibim); named among the princes in the Hekhalot lists.

raqiaf.def: An OCR/manuscript variant of Raqia, the firmament and the second of the seven heavens.

sagnesakiel.def: Sagnesakiel (Segansakkiel), the Prince of Wisdom, keeper of the treasuries of wisdom and understanding, counted among Metatron's own names in the Hekhalot tradition.

sagnezagiel.def: A spelling of Sagnesakiel, the Prince of Wisdom (also given as one of Metatron's names).

sammael.def: Sammael, the chief of the accusing angels (the satans) and the guardian prince of Rome/Esau, the great adversary who indicts Israel before the heavenly court (3 Enoch 14; 26).

samuil.def: A Slavonic form of the name (Samuil), appearing in the transmission of 2 Enoch; corresponds to a Hebrew Shemu'el.

sar torah.def: 'Prince of the Torah' (Sar Torah), the angelic office (held by Yephiphyah and invoked in the Sar Torah traditions) of the prince who bestows knowledge and retention of the Law upon the worthy.

segansakkiel.def: Segansakkiel, the Prince of Wisdom, a name also numbered among the seventy names of Metatron.

shachaqiel.def: Shachaqiel (Shahaqiel), one of the seven great princes each appointed over one of the seven heavens (3 Enoch 17).

shahaqiel.def: A spelling of Shachaqiel, one of the seven great princes set over the seven heavens (3 Enoch 17).

shalgiel.def: Shalgiel, the prince set over snow (sheleg) among the weather-princes (3 Enoch 14).

shallishim.def: 'Captains / officers' (from shalish, a third-tier commander), an order among the angelic army.

shataqiel.def: A spelling of Shatqiel, one of the seven great princes set over the seven heavens (3 Enoch 17).

shatqiel.def: Shatqiel, one of the seven great princes each appointed over one of the seven heavens, marshalling the host of his heaven (3 Enoch 17).

she'ol.def: Sheol, the underworld/abode of the dead in the biblical and Enochic cosmology.

shehaqim.def: Shehaqim, the third of the seven heavens, where the manna is ground for the righteous and the millstones of heaven turn.

shimshiel.def: Shimshiel (Samsiel), the prince set over the day/sun (shemesh), one of the luminary-princes (3 Enoch 14; 17).

shin'anim.def: The Shin'anim, an angelic order derived from Psalm 68:18 ('thousands upon thousands'), named among the hosts of heaven in the Hekhalot ranks.

sidriel.def: Sidriel, one of the seven great princes each set over one of the seven heavens (3 Enoch 17), named as prince of the first heaven.

soferiel.def: A spelling of Sopheriel YHWH, the recording prince who keeps the books of the living and the dead.

tafsarim.def: 'Marshals / commanders' (from the Akkadian tupsarru, scribe/officer), an angelic order named in 3 Enoch 14:1 among the ranks trembling before Metatron.

tebel.def: 'Tebel', the inhabited/productive world, one of the names of the earth in the cosmological lists of the Enoch and rabbinic traditions.

tumiel.def: Tumiel, one of the angelic princes named in the Hekhalot lists of the halls; office uncertain.

tutresiel.def: Tutresiel YHWH, one of the great guardian princes stationed over the halls of the Merkabah in Araboth (3 Enoch 18).

yehod.def: A component of the full divine name Akatriel Yah Yehod Sebaoth, a form of the Tetragrammaton used in the Hekhalot naming of the enthroned Glory.

yephiphyah.def: Yephiphyah (Yefefiah), the Prince of the Torah (Sar Torah) who reveals the secrets of the Law to those found worthy in the Hekhalot tradition.

yeshiba.def: The heavenly Yeshivah/academy, the celestial assembly where Torah is studied and where the righteous and the angels sit before the Presence.

yhwh ha-qatan.def: 'The lesser YHWH' (YHWH ha-Qatan), the astonishing title given to Metatron in 3 Enoch 12:5, marking him as bearing the Name and acting as God's vice-regent.

yophiel.def: Yophiel (Yofiel), a great prince associated with beauty and with the Torah/wisdom, named among the exalted angels of the Presence.

yophphiel.def: A spelling of Yophiel/Yofiel, the prince associated with divine beauty and wisdom.

za'amiel.def: Za'amiel, the prince set over vehemence/storm-fury (za'am) among the princes of the powers (3 Enoch 14).

zakzakiel.def: Zakzakiel YHWH, the prince appointed to record the merits of Israel upon the throne of Glory (3 Enoch 27).

zazriel.def: Zazriel YHWH, the prince of might/strength named among the guardian princes of the heavenly gates (3 Enoch 18).

zdaphiel.def: An OCR variant of Zaaphiel, the prince over hurricane/tempest.

zehanpuryu.def: Zehanpuryu YHWH, a most exalted prince who is honoured above Rikbiel and set over the powers of the Merkabah, of terrifying majesty (3 Enoch 18).

zi'iel.def: Zi'iel, the prince set over commotion/quaking movement (zi'a), one of the princes of the natural upheavals (3 Enoch 14).

ziqiel.def: Ziqiel, the prince set over comets/sparks and shooting stars (ziqin), one of the cosmic princes (3 Enoch 14).

ziz.def: The Ziz, the gigantic primordial bird of rabbinic legend (companion to Behemoth and Leviathan), lord of the birds whose wings darken the sun.
