shaddai.def: Shaddai — 'the Almighty', a name of God (El Shaddai); its gematria (314) equals that of Metatron.

rabba.def: Rabba — Aramaic 'the Great / great one', an honorific applied to a master or to the Divine.

lifegiver.def: 'Life-giver' — an epithet of God as the fountain and giver of life.

bareqet.def: Bareqet — the emerald/beryl, the third stone of the high priest's breastplate (Exodus 28:17); the name means 'flashing/lightning-stone'.

torateka.def: Toratekha — Hebrew 'your Torah / your Law', the instruction of God.

gabish.def: El-gabish — 'crystal / great hail-stones' (Ezekiel 13:11); the hard, icy stones of judgment.

esh.def: Esh — Hebrew 'fire', the elemental fire of which the angels and the river of fire (nehar di-nur) are made.

emeq.def: Emeq — Hebrew 'valley / depth', used of the depths of understanding or the deep places.

shoqed.def: Shoqed (Shoqed Chozi) — 'the watchful one', one of the angelic princes/names of the guardians in the Hekhalot texts.

quicksightedness.def: Quick-sightedness — keenness or sharpness of sight and perception.

storeplaces.def: Store-places — the heavenly storehouses/treasuries where snow, hail, dew, and the deeds of souls are kept (cf. the storehouses of 1 Enoch 60; 2 Enoch).

ashruylu.def: Ashruylu — one of the esoteric names of God/of the Prince invoked in the Hekhalot Sar-Torah rite of 3 Enoch, a permutation of the Divine Name.

arakiba.def: Second-named leader of the fallen Watchers in the list of chiefs of tens (1 En 6:7), also rendered Araqiba. His specific art is not detailed in Enoch.

rameel.def: Third-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7). Name likely means 'thunder of God' or 'morning of God'; distinct from Ramiel later in the same list.

kokabel.def: Fallen Watcher whose name means 'star of God'. He taught men the constellations (1 En 8:3). Listed among the twenty chiefs (spelled Kokabiel in 6:7) and again in the fuller list (69:2).

tamiel.def: Fifth-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7). Name possibly 'perfection of God'; his taught art is not specified.

ramiel.def: Sixth-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7), name meaning 'thunder of God'. Not to be confused with the archangel Remiel of chapter 20.

danel.def: Seventh-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7). Name means 'God is my judge'. Distinct from the later Watcher Danjal in 69:2.

ezeqeel.def: Fallen Watcher who taught men the knowledge of the clouds (1 En 8:3). Listed among the twenty chiefs (6:7). Name related to 'strength of God'.

baraqijal.def: Fallen Watcher whose name means 'lightning of God'. He taught astrology (1 En 8:3). Listed among the twenty chiefs (6:7); appears again as Baraqel in the fuller list (69:2).

asael.def: Tenth-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7). Widely identified with Azazel, who taught weapon-making and cosmetics; name means 'God has made' or 'God is doing'.

batarel.def: Twelfth-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7). Meaning of the name is uncertain; possibly 'rain of God' or related to being cut off. Distinct from Batarjal in 69:2.

ananel.def: Thirteenth-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7). Name means 'God is gracious' (cf. Hananel). Appears as Hananel in the fuller list of 69:2.

zaqiel.def: Fourteenth-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7). Name of uncertain meaning, possibly 'purity of God' or connected to storm/hail.

samsapeel.def: Fifteenth-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7). Name may relate to the sun (shamash). Appears as Simapesiel in 69:2.

satarel.def: Sixteenth-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7). Name possibly means 'hidden one of God' (from a root meaning to conceal).

jomjael.def: Nineteenth-named leader of the fallen Watchers (1 En 6:7). Name possibly means 'day of God'.

araqiel.def: Fallen Watcher who taught men the signs of the earth (1 En 8:3), i.e. earth-omens or geomancy. Name means 'earth of God'.

shamsiel.def: Fallen Watcher who taught men the signs of the sun (1 En 8:3), i.e. solar omens. Name means 'sun of God' (from shamash).

saraqael.def: One of the seven holy archangels, set over the spirits who sin in the spirit (1 En 20:6). Name of uncertain meaning, possibly 'command of God'.

artaqifa.def: Second-named fallen Watcher in the fuller list of 1 En 69:2. Name of uncertain meaning; possibly 'strong earth'.

armen.def: Third-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Meaning of the name is uncertain.

turael.def: Fifth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Possibly a variant of Turel; name may mean 'mountain of God'.

rumjal.def: Sixth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Name possibly means 'exalted one of God'. Compare Rumael later in the same list.

danjal.def: Seventh-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Name means 'God is my judge'; a variant/doublet of Danel.

neqael.def: Eighth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Meaning of the name is uncertain.

baraqel.def: Ninth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2, name meaning 'lightning of God'. A variant of Baraqijal, the Watcher who taught astrology.

batarjal.def: Twelfth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Name of uncertain meaning; a variant of Batarel from the earlier list.

busasejal.def: Thirteenth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2 (also spelled Busasejal/Busasejail). Meaning of the name is uncertain.

hananel.def: Fourteenth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Name means 'God is gracious'; a variant of Ananel from the earlier list.

simapesiel.def: Sixteenth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Meaning uncertain; a variant/expansion of Samsapeel.

jetrel.def: Seventeenth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Name possibly means 'abundance of God' (cf. Yeter/Jethro).

tumael.def: Eighteenth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Meaning of the name is uncertain.

rumael.def: Twentieth-named fallen Watcher in the list of 1 En 69:2. Name possibly means 'exalted one of God'; compare Rumjal.

jeqon.def: The first of the chief corrupters (1 En 69:4): the one who led astray all the sons of God, brought them down to the earth and led them astray through the daughters of men. His name is linked to a root meaning to be established or to cause to rebel.

asbeel.def: The second corrupter (1 En 69:5): he imparted evil counsel to the holy sons of God and led them astray so that they defiled their bodies with the daughters of men. Name possibly means 'deserter of God' or 'thought of God'.

gadreel.def: The third corrupter (1 En 69:6): he showed mankind all the blows of death, led Eve astray, and revealed the weapons of war — the shield, the coat of mail and the sword. Name possibly means 'help of God' or 'wall of God'.

penemue.def: The fourth corrupter (1 En 69:8): he taught men the bitter and the sweet and the secrets of wisdom, and instructed mankind in writing with ink and paper, by which many sinned. Name possibly means 'the inside/hidden' (cf. penim).

kasdeja.def: The fifth corrupter (1 En 69:12): he showed mankind the wicked smitings of spirits and demons, the smiting of the embryo in the womb to cause miscarriage, the bites of the serpent, and the smitings of the noontide heat. Name recalls the Chaldeans (Kasdim).

tabaet.def: Named in 1 En 69:12 as 'the son of the serpent named Tabaet', associated with the noontide-heat smiting revealed by Kasdeja. It denotes a serpent-demon or the offspring of the serpent; the exact meaning is uncertain.

kasbeel.def: The chief of the oath (1 En 69:13), who when he dwelt on high in glory revealed the oath to the holy ones; his name is given as Biqa. He requested Michael to show him the hidden name for use in the oath. Name linked to a root meaning to lie/deceive.

biqa.def: The alternate name of Kasbeel, the chief of the oath (1 En 69:13): 'its name is Biqa'. It designates the oath-angel or the oath itself; meaning uncertain, perhaps connected to a root for splitting/dividing.

akae.def: The name of the mighty oath which Kasbeel placed in the hand of Michael (1 En 69:15). It is the powerful oath by which the heaven, earth, sea, sun, moon and stars are held to their courses. Also rendered Akae/Akatha; meaning uncertain.

orjares.def: The first of the two names of the sun (1 En 78:1), the other being Tomas. It is one of the secret names of the great luminary that governs the day.

tomas.def: The second of the two names of the sun (1 En 78:1), paired with Orjares. One of the sun's secret names in Enoch's astronomy.

asonja.def: The first of the four names of the moon (1 En 78:2), followed by Ebla, Benase and Erae. A secret name of the lesser luminary that governs the night.

ebla.def: The second of the four names of the moon (1 En 78:2). One of the moon's secret names in Enoch's astronomical section.

benase.def: The third of the four names of the moon (1 En 78:2). One of the moon's secret names in Enoch's astronomy.

erae.def: The fourth of the four names of the moon (1 En 78:2), last after Asonja, Ebla and Benase. One of the moon's secret names.

milkiel.def: The first of the four leaders (season-leaders) who divide the four parts of the year (1 En 82:13, spelled Milkiel). At the beginning of the year Melkejal rises first and rules, named Tam'aini and 'sun'; his dominion is ninety-one days (82:15). Name means 'king of God' or 'my king is God'.

helemmelek.def: The second of the four season-leaders of the year (1 En 82:13, 82:18), whom one names 'the shining sun'; his period of rule is ninety-one days marked by glowing heat and the ripening of fruits. Name may mean 'strength of the king' or 'health of the king'.

melejal.def: The third of the four season-leaders who divide the four parts of the year (1 En 82:13). Name possibly means 'fullness of God' or a variant of the royal 'melek' element.

narel.def: The fourth of the four season-leaders who divide the four parts of the year (1 En 82:13). Name possibly means 'lamp/light of God' or 'boy of God'.

adnarel.def: One of three subordinate star-leaders who lead the season-leaders (1 En 82:14), following the leaders of the orders. Name of uncertain meaning, possibly 'lord/delight of God'.

ijasusael.def: One of the three subordinate star-leaders of the orders (1 En 82:14). Meaning of the name is uncertain.

elomeel.def: The third of the subordinate star-leaders of the orders (1 En 82:14). Name contains the divine element 'Elohim'; exact meaning uncertain.

tamaini.def: The alternate name of Melkejal, the first season-leader, at the start of the year: 'who is named Tam'aini and sun' (1 En 82:15). It designates the sun-aspect of the first quarter's ruler; meaning uncertain.

berkael.def: One of the star-leaders (heads of a thousand) under the season-leader in the first quarter (1 En 82:17). Name means 'blessing of God' or 'God has blessed'.

zelebsel.def: One of the star-leaders (heads of a thousand) under the season-leader in the first quarter (1 En 82:17). Meaning of the name is uncertain.

hilujaseph.def: A star-leader added as a head of a thousand under the first-quarter season-leader (1 En 82:17), with whom the days of that dominion end. Name of uncertain meaning; the 'joseph' element may echo 'may God add'.

gidaijal.def: One of the star-leaders, a head of a thousand, in the ordering of leaders under Helemmelek's quarter (1 En 82:20). Name possibly means 'troop/fortune of God'.

keel.def: One of the star-leaders (heads of thousands) listed in 1 En 82:20, alongside Gidaijal and Heel. Meaning of the short name is uncertain.

heel.def: One of the star-leaders (heads of thousands) listed in 1 En 82:20, alongside Gidaijal and Keel. Meaning of the short name is uncertain.

asfael.def: The star-leader added as head of a thousand in 1 En 82:20, with whom the days of that dominion end. Name of uncertain meaning, possibly 'gathering of God'.

tartarus.def: The abyss/underworld over which the archangel Uriel is set (1 En 20:2). A Greek term for the deep place of punishment, adopted in Enoch for the prison of the wicked and the fallen.

abelsjail.def: Abel-Main (Abelsjail), the place to the south-west of Hermon, between Lebanon and Senir, where Enoch sat and read out the petition of the Watchers (1 En 13:9). A watered plain-place associated with weeping/mourning (abel).

lebanon.def: The mountain range named as one bound of the region of Abel-Main where Enoch received his visions (1 En 13:9). Name means 'white', from its snow-capped heights.

senir.def: The Amorite name for Mount Hermon (or a peak of it), named with Lebanon as bounding the place of Abel-Main in Enoch's vision (1 En 13:9).

kruno.def: The planet placed in the first and highest circle of the heavens on the fourth day of creation (2 En 30:3). Kruno is Kronos, the Greek name for the planet Saturn, outermost of the seven classical planetary bodies.

aphrodite.def: The planet placed in the second circle of the heavens (2 En 30:3). Aphrodite is the Greek name for the planet Venus, the morning/evening star.

aris.def: The planet of the third circle in the ordering of the seven classical planets (2 En 30:3, whose primary text is lost in this source but restored from the standard 2 Enoch planetary order). Aris is Ares, the Greek name for the planet Mars.

zeus.def: The planet placed in the fifth circle of the heavens (2 En 30:6). Zeus is the Greek name for the planet Jupiter, greatest of the classical planets.

hermes.def: The planet placed in the sixth circle of the heavens (2 En 30:6). Hermes is the Greek name for the planet Mercury, swiftest of the planets.

riman.def: One of Enoch's kinsmen summoned by Methosalem, together with the elders of the people, to receive Enoch's blessing and last words (2 En 57:2).

ukhan.def: One of Enoch's kinsmen called before Enoch prior to his departure, listed among the brethren of Methosalem (2 En 57:2).

sonofman.def: The exalted heavenly figure of the Similitudes (1 En 69:26-29), whose name is revealed to the righteous and who is seated on the throne of glory to judge sinners and those who led the world astray. A messianic title meaning 'the Son of Man'.

lordofspirits.def: The characteristic Enochic title for God throughout the Similitudes (e.g. 1 En 69:24), before whom all creation gives thanks and by whose oath the cosmos is upheld. It designates the Most High as sovereign over the hosts of heaven.
